vat_rates.note: Temporary zero rate for retrofitting a battery that stores electricity from a microgeneration system, and for standalone batteries storing grid electricity, in residential accommodation.
Reduced rate of 5% after the temporary zero rate ends (HMRC Notice 708/6: energy-saving materials revert to 5% from 1 April 2027).
Temporary zero rate for installing solar panels in residential accommodation.
Reverts to the reduced rate of 5% from 1 April 2027 (scheduled; confirmed again in the Budget 2026 overview of tax legislation and rates). A change in law would need a new row.

cost_ranges.note: One battery = the 6-10.99 kWh retrofit band, 2025/26: median GBP 890/kWh (n = 14,457, DESNZ rounds to the nearest GBP 10) x 9.8 kWh average capacity of that band (141,650 kWh total / 14,457 installs) = GBP 8,722. Existing homes only; includes equipment, installation and VAT where applicable (batteries were zero-rated throughout 2025/26, so treated as ex-VAT; VAT on the install date is added separately). DESNZ gives no interval, so low and high are null and the engine adds +/- the missing-range spread and labels them estimated. Other bands (median per kWh, 2025/26): 1-5.99 kWh GBP 1,300; 11-29.99 kWh GBP 630.

Range built only from published DESNZ/MCS 2025/26 GB figures (TIC basis, per kW of total installed capacity, battery excluded, Northern Ireland excluded): low = median of all 4-10 kW installs, GBP 1,545.89/kW; likely = mean of all domestic installs, GBP 1,772.43/kW (sheet Domestic costs); high = mean of domestic retrofit 0-4 kW installs, GBP 2,108.65/kW (sheet New build costs). Divided by 1,000 to give GBP per watt. Small systems cost more per kW than large ones, so the high end is the small-system retrofit mean. Figures include VAT where applicable; domestic solar was zero-rated throughout 2025/26, so they are treated as ex-VAT and VAT on the install date is added separately. Not a quote: installer prices vary. Next DESNZ release: 27 May 2027.
cost_ranges.unit: GBP per watt DC (DESNZ GBP per kW / 1,000)

export_policies.note: For people whose electricity is not supplied by British Gas. Variable rate.

export_policy_rates.note: 3 pence per kWh exported, as published by British Gas on 2026-11-22.

export_policies.note: Only for existing EDF residential electricity customers. A 1-year fixed tariff; the rate after the first year is not published.

export_policy_rates.note: 13 pence per kWh exported, as published by EDF on 2026-11-22.

export_policies.name: EDF SEG Export Variable
export_policies.note: Open to anyone. Cut from 3.0p to 2.0p per kWh on 28 October 2026.

export_policies.note: Variable rate, open to new and existing E.ON Next customers with a renewable system up to 5 MW. Needs a smart export meter.

export_policies.name: Outgoing Octopus (variable)
export_policies.note: Variable rate. Only for Octopus import customers, paired with certain import tariffs. Needs a smart meter that records half-hourly export.

export_policy_rates.note: 12 pence per kWh exported, as published by Octopus Energy on 2026-11-22.

export_policies.name: Octopus Smart Export Guarantee (fixed)
export_policies.note: Open to anyone: you can keep a different supplier for your import. Needs MCS (or equivalent) certification and a smart meter that records half-hourly export.

export_policy_rates.note: 4.1 pence per kWh exported, as published by Octopus Energy on 2026-11-22.

export_policies.name: OVO Smart Export Guarantee
export_policies.note: Open to anyone, whoever supplies your electricity. Needs MCS (or equivalent) certification and a smart meter.

export_policy_rates.note: 4 pence per kWh exported, as published by OVO on 2026-11-22.

model_assumptions.rationale: PVGIS system losses (the key keeps its legacy name). 14% is the PVGIS default system loss and is what every GB yield figure on the site uses; 20% (some shade) and 30% (heavy shade) are product choices that step the loss up for partial and heavy shade. Not sourced.
Product choice: size the system to cover 80% to 100% of estimated annual usage, which gives the low and high ends of the suggested size range. Not sourced.
Product choice: the DESNZ/MCS cost data used for pricing stops at the 4-10 kW band for homes, so the suggested size is capped at 10 kW rather than priced outside the data. Not sourced.
Product choice: below this a payback figure is not meaningful for a rooftop installation, so the calculator warns instead. Not sourced.
Input sanity limit for the monthly bill field, so a typing slip (an extra zero) is caught. Not sourced.
Product choice: 0.5% less output each year, a conventional planning figure for crystalline silicon panels. Not sourced; replace with a datasheet or published study value if the owner prefers.
Product choice: a 25-year projection with no discounting, the same horizon as the US calculator. Inverter and battery replacement are not modelled.

Product choice: where a source gives a likely value but no bounds (the battery cost and each export rate), low and high are likely -/+ 15% and the result says they are estimated. Placeholder until bounds are sourced.
Product choice: electricity prices flat (low), rising 2% a year (likely) or 4% a year (high). Not a forecast; the Ofgem cap changes every quarter and can fall as well as rise.

model_assumptions.unit: fraction of solar output used at home
model_assumptions.rationale: NO PRIMARY SOURCE FOUND (listed in docs/TODO-VERIFY.md). A deliberately wide product-choice range: how much of the solar output is used in the home rather than exported depends on when the household is at home. Secondary guides (for example Uswitch, about 30% without a battery and 70% or more with one; Utilita citing the MCS procedure at 54%) were read as context only. Replace with a primary figure when one is found.

Derived from 12 PVGIS 5.3 runs (1 kWp, 35 degree tilt, 14% losses, PVGIS-SARAH3) for London, Manchester and Edinburgh, in the research pack: yield facing east, west or north divided by yield facing south. East/west ratios: London 0.802 / 0.773, Manchester 0.810 / 0.792, Edinburgh 0.780 / 0.776 (low = smallest, high = largest, likely = mean of the six). North: 0.531, 0.558, 0.523 (likely = mean). South-facing yield itself comes live from PVGIS at the optimal tilt. Only the likely factor feeds the calculation; low and high are shown as the spread. Source runs: https://re.jrc.ec.europa.eu/api/v5_3/PVcalc?lat=51.5072&lon=-0.1275&peakpower=1&loss=14&angle=35&aspect=-90&outputformat=json (aspect=0 south, -90 east, 90 west, 180 north; same pattern for each city).
